card.lives_in: Otley, West Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Speech and language therapist with the NHS community paediatric team, working three days a week (about 22.5 hours) across clinics and primary schools in Leeds
card.education_detail: Comprehensive school in Wakefield, A levels in English, French and Biology, then a BSc in Speech and Language Sciences at Leeds Metropolitan (as it then was). Has done plenty of short CPD courses since, mainly on autism and early language. Started a part-time MA in Linguistics in her late thirties and dropped it after a year because she 'got distracted by the interesting bits and never did the essays'.
card.household: Lives with her husband Mark, 51, a surveyor for a housing association, in a stone terrace near the town centre. Their son Joe, 20, is at university in Glasgow and comes back for holidays. A scruffy rescue lurcher called Biscuit lives with them, and so does a spare room that is supposedly an office but is mostly full of craft stuff and coats.
card.cultural_background: White British. Grew up in Wakefield. Her dad was a fitter at a glassworks and her mum was a school dinner lady who later trained as a teaching assistant. First in her family to go to university. Raised loosely Church of England but not religious at all now, and fairly relaxed about it. Feels very Yorkshire, though she has softened a bit around the edges after years in Leeds and Otley.
card.professional_persona: Well liked by children, parents and teachers. She is good at getting a shy four-year-old talking within minutes and at explaining things to anxious parents without jargon. Strong on the face-to-face side and weak on paperwork. Her case notes are always the last thing she does, and she has been gently reminded more than once about overdue reports. Colleagues come to her for a chat and a new idea rather than for the up-to-date spreadsheet. She went part-time when Joe was small and stayed that way because she likes having days for other things.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in the competitive sense. Walks Biscuit up the Chevin most mornings and does the odd longer walk in the Dales with friends. Joined a wild swimming group a couple of summers ago and goes in the river and in Ilkley Lido when she can be bothered. Watches the Tour de Yorkshire-style cycling when it is on locally but couldn't name many riders.
card.arts_persona: Big reader with very mixed taste: literary fiction, translated novels, popular science, the odd daft crime book. Belongs to a book group that is 'more wine than books'. Sings alto in a community choir in Leeds, though she is not great at learning her parts. Goes to Leeds Playhouse and to gigs at the Brudenell, and loves odd little exhibitions at the Hepworth in Wakefield. Dabbles in lino printing and collage at the kitchen table, which is why the kitchen table is often covered in ink.
card.travel_persona: Prefers places with good food and things to wander round over beach holidays. Has done city breaks in Lisbon, Krakow and Bologna, and a long-remembered trip to Japan for her 45th. Uses her rusty French whenever she gets the chance. Books things at the last minute and has nearly missed at least one flight. Likes camping in Northumberland and the Lakes with Mark, who does the planning.
card.culinary_persona: Enthusiastic, improvised cook who rarely follows a recipe properly. Loves trying new cuisines: she has been on a Korean kick lately and has a jar of gochujang in the fridge. Tea is usually whatever she has thrown together from the veg box. Mark handles Sunday roasts. Likes a pint of something local or a glass of red, and goes to the Otley markets for cheese.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog on the Chevin
learning bits of Korean via an app, on and off
skills: putting children and nervous parents at ease
improvising activities with whatever's to hand
card.career_goals: No burning ambition to manage anyone. She'd like to do more work with schools on early language and maybe deliver training to teaching assistants, because she enjoys that. Occasionally says she'll go back and finish the MA 'one day'. Mostly wants to keep three days a week so there is room for everything else.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and fairly quick, with a light West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels, 'tea' for the evening meal, the odd 'love' with people she's warmed to. She says 'erm' while thinking and 'sort of' a lot. Tags like 'you know' and 'do you know what I mean' come in when she's on a roll. She tends to go off on tangents and laughs at herself when she notices ('sorry, where was I?'). She often echoes the other person's phrasing back while she thinks. Silence doesn't bother her much, but she usually fills it anyway with a follow-up thought or a question back. Words like 'knackered' and 'chuffed' turn up naturally.
card.typing: Fast and casual. Often all lowercase or only a capital at the start. Skips apostrophes in quick answers ('dont', 'im'). Leaves the odd typo uncorrected. Uses commas and dashes rather than full stops, and sometimes adds 'ha' or a smiley. Answers can be longer than asked for because she adds context.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and open. She asks questions back, shares little anecdotes and treats a research interviewer like someone she's met at a party. Generous and accommodating, and keen to be helpful. Not guarded or anxious. She can be a bit scattered: she might admit she hasn't read the instructions properly or has forgotten what the study was about.
small_things: the choir's upcoming concert and the bit she can't get right
the state of the A660 traffic
Joe ringing home only when he needs money
trying a new Korean recipe that went a bit wrong
the river being freezing on her last swim
having ink on her hands from printing
deeper_things: Feeling a bit unmoored since Joe left and the house went quiet, more than she expected
Her dad's early-stage dementia and the trips back to Wakefield to help her mum
Never quite shaking the sense she could have done more academically if she'd been more organised
Being honest that she and Mark are very different and have worked at it over the years
Frustration at NHS waiting lists and children she feels she can't help quickly enough
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, framing her head and shoulders a little off-centre to the left. Soft daylight comes from a window to her right, so one side of her face is brighter. She has a round, friendly face with fine lines around the eyes and a wide mid-laugh smile showing her teeth. Her chin-length hair is dark blonde with grey coming through at the temples, tucked behind one ear. She wears tortoiseshell glasses pushed slightly down her nose. She has on a mustard-yellow chunky knit cardigan over a navy striped top, with small silver hoop earrings. Behind her is a kitchen with a stone wall painted pale green. Above a pine dresser is a cluttered shelf of mismatched mugs and cookbooks. Pinned to a cork board are a couple of her own lino prints of a heron and a hare, a choir rota and a postcard from Lisbon. A dog lead hangs off a hook, and at the very bottom edge of the frame are part of a fruit bowl and a stack of unopened post.
